question_text: Does the product still have hair, fur or wool on the hide, or has the hair been removed?

value_labels.leather: Leather only - hair/wool has been removed (smooth tanned hide)
value_labels.furskin: Furskin - hide still has hair, fur or wool attached (mink, fox, rabbit, sheepskin with wool, etc.)
value_labels.artificial_fur: Artificial fur - imitation fur made by gumming/sewing hair onto a backing (NOT knitted/woven imitations)

notes: Disambiguates Ch.42 (leather) vs Ch.43 (furskin/fur). Ch.43 Note 1 defines furskin as 'tanned or dressed with the hair or wool on'. The hair-on/hair-off distinction is the legal bright line.

question_text: What is the main material of the garment or accessory?

value_labels.leather: Leather (cowhide, lambskin, etc.) or composition leather
value_labels.textile_woven: Textile fabric that is woven (e.g. cotton shirt, polyester suit)
value_labels.textile_knitted: Textile fabric that is knitted or crocheted (e.g. T-shirt, sweater)
value_labels.synthetic_leather: Synthetic / faux leather (PU- or PVC-coated fabric, plastic surface)

notes: Disambiguates Ch.42 (leather apparel 4203) vs Ch.61/62 (textile apparel). Faux leather routes to Ch.39 or Ch.62 depending on coating thickness; treat as textile branch for this question.

question_text: Which broad material family best describes the product?

value_labels.metal: Metal (iron / steel / aluminium / copper / brass / other base metal)
value_labels.natural_origin: Natural material (wood, leather, textile, paper, cork, stone)
value_labels.other_inorganic: Other (glass, ceramic, mineral, chemical, or composite — please describe)

notes: Universal material discriminator (4-bucket top level). Used when info-gain on `material` ranks highest across candidates. Refined by chapter-scoped templates (e.g. predominant_element for Ch.72-81, textile-specific for Ch.50-53).

question_text: Which metal makes up most of the product by weight?

value_labels.iron: Iron or steel (Fe) — including stainless and alloy steels
value_labels.other_base_metal: Other base metal (nickel, zinc, tin, lead, titanium, tungsten, magnesium, etc.) — please specify in next step

notes: Used when product is clearly metallic but the chapter (72-81) needs disambiguation. Maps to predominant_element internally. 'other_base_metal' triggers a follow-up template (`predominant_element` chapter-specific) for further refinement.

question_text: What type of leather is the product made from?

value_labels.full_grain_leather: Full-grain or top-grain leather (intact natural surface)
value_labels.split_leather: Split leather or suede (under-layer of the hide)
value_labels.composition_leather: Composition leather / bonded leather (bonded leather fibres)

notes: Refines material within Ch.42 (heading 4115 vs 4203 vs 4107 etc.). Optional; only invoked when Ch.42 candidates span multiple leather sub-types.

question_text: What is the physical form of the product as exported?

value_labels.raw_bulk: Raw bulk material (granules, powder, lump, ingot, billet)
value_labels.semi_finished: Semi-finished shape (sheet, plate, strip, foil, wire, rod, bar, tube, pipe)
value_labels.finished_part: Finished part or component ready for use / assembly
value_labels.complete_product: Complete product / machine / appliance ready for end-use
value_labels.fabric_or_yarn: Fabric, yarn, fibre or textile material

notes: Universal form bucket. Helps separate raw-material chapters from semi-finished and finished-good chapters.

question_text: Is the synthetic / artificial fibre continuous (filament) or cut into short lengths (staple)?

value_labels.filament: Continuous filament - one long strand of indefinite length (filament yarn, monofilament, multifilament)
value_labels.staple: Staple - short cut lengths typically 20-150 mm (cut staple, carded or combed staple fibre)
value_labels.tow_long: Filament tow longer than 2 metres (treated as filament - Ch.54)
value_labels.tow_short: Filament tow 2 metres or shorter (treated as staple - Ch.55)

notes: Disambiguates Ch.54 (filament) vs Ch.55 (staple). Ch.55 Note 1: tow >2m = filament side; ≤2m = staple side. Same chemistry, form decides.

question_text: What metallurgical shape is the product?

value_labels.ingot_billet: Ingot, billet, slab or other primary cast form
value_labels.finished_article: Finished article (fastener, hand tool, fitting, container, etc.)

notes: Within metal chapters, the heading is largely determined by form. Heading 7208-7212 (flat-rolled) vs 7213-7217 (bars/rods/wire) vs 7304-7306 (tubes) etc.

question_text: How is the product presented to the buyer?

value_labels.bulk_powder: Bulk powder, crystals or granules in large containers (drums, sacks, IBCs)
value_labels.bulk_liquid: Bulk liquid in drums or tankers
value_labels.dosage_syrup_cream: Syrup, suspension, ointment, cream or other measured dosage form

notes: Disambiguates Ch.29 (bulk API) vs Ch.30 (formulated pharmaceutical). Once put up in measured doses or for retail sale, the product moves to Ch.30 (per Ch.29 Note 1).

question_text: What is the physical form of the coffee product?

value_labels.ground_bean: Ground coffee (still the roasted bean, just milled - needs brewing)
value_labels.soluble_powder: Soluble powder or granules that dissolve directly in water (instant coffee)

notes: Reinforces processing_state for Ch.09 vs Ch.21. Ground coffee (Ch.09) and instant coffee powder (Ch.21) can both look like 'powder' to a user; this question clarifies.

question_text: What is the primary function or purpose of the product?

value_labels.machine_or_equipment: Machine, mechanical or electrical equipment / appliance
value_labels.consumable_or_material: Consumable, food, chemical, or raw / processed material
value_labels.article_or_finished_goods: Finished article — apparel, container, tool, furniture, decorative or household item
value_labels.part_or_component: Part, component or accessory of a larger product (please describe what it goes into)

notes: Universal function discriminator (4-bucket top level). Used when the candidate set spans multiple Sections. Refined by chapter-scoped function templates (Ch.84/85, Ch.73/82/83, Ch.38, Ch.09/21).

question_text: What is the main role of the machine or appliance?

value_labels.mechanical_processing: Mechanical processing - pump, compressor, engine, turbine, motor, hydraulic/pneumatic
value_labels.production_machine: Production machinery - machine tool, textile machine, food-processing machine, printing press
value_labels.electrical_generation: Electrical generation, conversion or distribution (transformers, generators, switchgear)
value_labels.electronic_device: Electronic device - communication, computing, control, signal processing
value_labels.domestic_appliance: Domestic / household appliance (washing machine, refrigerator, microwave)

notes: Disambiguates within Ch.84/85. Engines and mechanical parts stay in Ch.84 even when vehicle-destined (Section XVII Note 2(e)).

question_text: What is the primary function of this metal article?

value_labels.hand_tool_cutting: Hand tool with a cutting / chiselling / drilling action (Ch.82)
value_labels.fastener: Fastener - bolt, screw, nut, rivet, washer, nail
value_labels.fitting_fixture: Fitting or fixture - hinge, lock, hook, bracket, mounting
value_labels.structural_part: Structural part - tube, pipe, plate, structural section ready for use
value_labels.kitchenware_household: Kitchenware, household article or sanitary ware
value_labels.container: Container, drum, tank or pressurised vessel

notes: Disambiguates within base-metal Section XV. Hand tools route to Ch.82; misc base-metal articles to Ch.83; structural to Ch.73-76 depending on metal.

question_text: Where will the product mainly be used?

value_labels.vehicle_or_transport: For motor vehicles, aircraft, ships, railways or other transport
value_labels.household_personal: Household, personal or wearable use (clothing, footwear, kitchenware, furniture)
value_labels.medical_or_specialised: Medical, dental, scientific, agricultural or other specialised end-use

notes: Universal intended_use bucket (4-bucket top level). Refined by chapter-scoped intended_use templates (Ch.84/85/87 vehicle test, Ch.30 therapeutic purpose, Ch.61/62/63 gender, Ch.71 precious metal, Ch.94 furniture, Ch.95 toy).

question_text: Is the part designed solely or principally for use in a motor vehicle?

value_labels.vehicle_specific: Yes - designed solely or principally for vehicles of Ch.87 (cars, trucks, buses, two-wheelers, tractors)
value_labels.general_industrial: No - it is general-purpose machinery usable across many applications
value_labels.engine_or_part_of_engine: It is an engine or an integral part of an engine (these always stay in Ch.84 even when vehicle-destined)
value_labels.bearing_valve_transmission: It is a ball/roller bearing, valve, or transmission shaft (these stay in Ch.84 even when vehicle-destined)

notes: Implements Section XVII Note 3 'solely or principally' test. Even vehicle-bound engines (8407/8408), bearings (8482), valves (8481), and transmission shafts (8483) stay in Ch.84. chapter_exclusion ids 2424-2427.

question_text: Who is the garment intended for?

value_labels.unisex_or_industrial: Unisex, workwear, or industrial / technical use

notes: Within apparel Ch.61/62, gender split drives the heading (e.g. 6103 men's vs 6104 women's suits). Babies' garments have a dedicated heading 6111/6209.

question_text: What is the therapeutic purpose of the pharmaceutical?

value_labels.therapeutic_human: Therapeutic or prophylactic for human use
value_labels.diagnostic: Diagnostic reagent or in-vitro diagnostic kit
value_labels.wound_care: Wound dressing, plaster, bandage or related

notes: Within Ch.30, the heading (3001 vs 3002 vs 3003 vs 3004 vs 3005 vs 3006) is partly driven by therapeutic purpose.

question_text: What is the processing state of the product?

value_labels.raw_unprocessed: Raw or unprocessed (e.g. fresh, untanned, unrefined, crude)
value_labels.semi_processed: Semi-processed (e.g. dried, frozen, hot-rolled, tanned, refined)
value_labels.finished: Fully finished and ready for use
value_labels.formulated_or_mixed: Formulated, mixed, or compounded (e.g. retail-ready preparation)

notes: Universal processing-state bucket. Useful for separating raw-material chapters (Ch.01-15, 25-27, 41, 44, 50-53) from finished-product chapters.

question_text: Has the coffee been extracted (water/solvent extraction to produce instant/soluble coffee), or is it still in bean or ground form?

value_labels.roasted_bean: Roasted bean or ground roasted coffee (still requires brewing)
value_labels.decaffeinated_bean: Decaffeinated roasted bean or ground (still Ch.09 - only the caffeine was extracted)
value_labels.extracted_soluble: Extract, essence or concentrate - dissolves directly in water (instant / soluble coffee)
value_labels.preparation_with_coffee: Preparation with a basis of coffee extract (3-in-1 mix, coffee+milk powder, coffee+sugar)

notes: Disambiguates Ch.09 (roasted/ground bean) vs Ch.21 (extracts and preparations of extracts). Decaffeination is Ch.09-resident because only the caffeine was extracted, not the coffee solids.

question_text: Is the chemical compound in unformulated bulk form, or has it been formulated for end-use?

value_labels.bulk_unformulated: Bulk unformulated API or chemical (powder/crystal/granules in industrial packs)
value_labels.stabilised_or_in_water_transport: Bulk with a minor stabiliser, anti-caking agent, or dissolved in water purely for safe transport
value_labels.formulated_dosage: Formulated dosage form - tablet, capsule, ampoule, vial, syrup, ointment
value_labels.retail_mixed_preparation: Mixed preparation in measured doses or retail pack (combination tablets, multivitamin formulas)

notes: Disambiguates Ch.29 (separate compound or near-pure with Note 1(d)-(g) carve-outs) vs Ch.30 (formulated medicament or mixed preparation). chapter_exclusion 2678 encodes the redirect.

question_text: What is the preservation or cooking state of the food product?

value_labels.dried_salted_smoked: Dried, salted, in brine, or smoked
value_labels.cooked_or_prepared: Cooked, otherwise prepared, or preserved (e.g. canned, marinated, breaded)

notes: Within food chapters, preservation state often drives the heading or sub-chapter (e.g. Ch.02/03 = fresh/frozen, Ch.16 = prepared/preserved meat/fish, Ch.20 = preserved vegetables/fruit).

question_text: How has the steel or iron product been rolled or worked?

value_labels.plated_or_coated: Plated or coated (zinc-galvanised, tin-coated tinplate, painted, plastic-coated)
value_labels.drawn_or_extruded: Drawn or extruded (cold-finished bars, drawn wire)

notes: Within Ch.72, sub-chapter heading routing depends on rolling/working state (7208 hot-rolled flat vs 7209 cold-rolled flat vs 7210 plated/coated flat).

question_text: Is the product made of a single material, or is it a combination of materials?

value_labels.single_material: Single material (e.g. all steel, all cotton, all polyester)
value_labels.composite_essential_character: Composite of two or more materials, but one clearly gives the product its essential character
value_labels.mixture_or_set: Mixture, set, or kit with no single dominant material
value_labels.coated_or_laminated: Layered, coated or laminated (one material gives the surface, another the substrate)

notes: Drives GIR-3(b) essential character analysis. Composite_components field is populated when one material is primary and others are secondary/auxiliary.

question_text: Is the product carbon steel, stainless steel, or another alloy steel?

value_labels.non_alloy_carbon_steel: Non-alloy / plain carbon steel (mostly Fe + C)
value_labels.other_alloy_steel: Other alloy steel (significant Cr, Ni, Mn, Mo, V, etc. but not stainless)
value_labels.iron_not_steel: Cast iron, pig iron, or other non-steel iron

notes: Within Ch.72, alloy class drives the heading (7208-7212 carbon, 7218-7223 stainless, 7224-7229 other alloy). Maps to chemical composition percentages populated by O2.

question_text: Is the garment made from knitted (or crocheted) fabric, or from woven fabric?

value_labels.knitted_or_crocheted: Yes - the fabric is knitted or crocheted (stretches, has visible loops; e.g. T-shirt, sweater, jersey)
value_labels.woven: No - the fabric is woven (rigid weave, e.g. dress shirt, denim, suiting fabric)
value_labels.non_woven: Non-woven (spunbond, felt, bonded fibre - treat as Ch.62)
value_labels.wadding_only: Wholly of wadding (e.g. quilted only, no outer shell)

notes: The exemplar binary discriminator: fully resolves Ch.61 vs Ch.62 except for heading 6212 (brassieres, etc.) which is always Ch.62. Note: 'non-woven' is in the 'not knit/crochet, not wadding' bucket = Ch.62.

question_text: How was the fabric constructed?

value_labels.woven: Woven (warp + weft interlaced on a loom)

notes: Within textile-fabric chapters (Ch.50-60), construction routes to specific chapter (woven Ch.50-55, knitted Ch.60, non-woven Ch.56).

question_text: Is the article a finished (made-up) item ready to use, or is it fabric on a roll?

value_labels.made_up_yes: Yes - made-up finished article (hemmed, sewn, assembled, ready to use - e.g. shirt, towel, curtain, bedsheet)
value_labels.made_up_no_fabric: No - it is fabric sold by the metre / on a bolt / roll (not hemmed or finished)

notes: Pre-filter for Ch.61/62/63. If made_up=false, the product is in Ch.50-60 fabric chapters. Boolean attribute.

question_text: Is the electrical/electronic item worn on the body, or used independently?

value_labels.wearable_yes: Yes - worn on the body (smart watch, hearing aid, wearable sensor band, headphones)
value_labels.wearable_no: No - used independently or fixed in place (TV, refrigerator, charger, lamp)

notes: Boolean attribute used for Ch.85 sub-routing where wearable status influences heading choice (e.g. hearing aids heading 9021 vs headphones 8518).

question_text: Does the product use electricity to provide heating as its primary function?

value_labels.electric_heating_primary: Yes - electric heating is the main function (electric blanket, heating pad, kettle, water heater)
value_labels.no_electric_heating: No - any electrical aspect is secondary (or the product has no electrical components)

notes: Boolean attribute. Distinguishes textile blanket (Ch.63) from electrically-heated blanket (Ch.85, heading 8516). Routes textile + electric → Ch.85.

question_text: Does the appliance generate heat electrically as its primary purpose?

value_labels.electric_heating_primary: Yes - electric heating is the main purpose (electric oven, toaster, iron, immersion heater, kettle)
value_labels.electric_heating_incidental: No - any heat is incidental to another primary purpose (motor warms up, IC chip warms up)

notes: Boolean attribute used to route electrothermic appliances to heading 8516 (electric heating appliances).

question_text: Is the chemical a single chemically-defined compound, a mixture of isomers, or a formulation/mixture?

value_labels.separate_inorganic_compound: Single inorganic compound (e.g. NaCl, H2SO4, CuSO4) - chapter Ch.28
value_labels.separate_organic_compound: Single organic compound (e.g. paracetamol, ethanol, glucose) - chapter Ch.29
value_labels.isomer_mixture: Mixture of isomers of the same compound (e.g. mixed xylenes) - still Ch.29
value_labels.sugar_derivative: Sugar ether, ester, or other sugar derivative - Ch.29 heading 2940
value_labels.diazonium_salt: Diazonium salt or coupling intermediate - Ch.29
value_labels.mixed_formulation: Mixture of different compounds, formulation, or preparation - NOT Ch.28/29 (likely Ch.30/32/33/35/38)

notes: Implements Ch.29 Note 1 eligibility tests. The chemical_class enum directly mirrors notes-claim sub-bullets.

question_text: Which metal predominates by weight in this product?

value_labels.iron: Iron / steel (Fe) — including all steels (carbon, stainless, alloy). NOTE: tin-coated steel sheet ('tinplate') is iron-predominant.
value_labels.copper_or_aluminium: Copper (Cu, including brass and bronze) or aluminium (Al)
value_labels.tin_zinc_lead_nickel: Tin (Sn ≥ 50%), zinc, lead, or nickel — please specify in next step which one
value_labels.other_base_metal: Other base metal (titanium, tungsten, magnesium, beryllium, antimony, etc.)

notes: Resolves Ch.72 vs Ch.80 trade-name confusion: 'tinplate' = tin-COATED steel sheet = Ch.72 (Fe predominant); pure tin metal = Ch.80 (Sn predominant). Section XV General Note 5 applies. The 'tin_zinc_lead_nickel' bucket triggers a follow-up specialisation if needed.

question_text: What is the role of the article in the final use?

value_labels.packaging: Packaging - container, bag, box, bottle to hold or protect another product
value_labels.structural_support: Structural or supporting role in an assembly (sheet, panel, profile)
value_labels.independent_product: An independent finished product (kitchenware, tableware, decorative object)
value_labels.technical_part: Technical part incorporated in machinery, apparatus or instrument

notes: Used for Ch.39 (plastics) and Ch.48 (paper) and Ch.70 (glass) where the role drives heading selection (e.g. plastic packaging 3923 vs plastic structural 3925 vs plastic kitchenware 3924).

question_text: What is the optical or instrument-related role of the product?
notes: Ch.90 is high-SKIP-risk; this template helps route within optical/precision instrument headings.

question_text: Is the organic compound supplied dissolved in a solvent (e.g. water, alcohol)?

value_labels.in_solution_no: No - solid (powder, crystal, granular) or neat liquid

notes: Combined with solution_purpose to apply Ch.29 Note 1(d)/(e) test. If in solution AND purpose=safety/transport → stays Ch.29; if purpose=specific_use → moves to Ch.30 (or other formulation chapter).

question_text: Why is the compound supplied in solution?

value_labels.safety_transport: For safe transport or storage only (e.g. concentrated formaldehyde in water; the solution is purely a handling convenience)
value_labels.specific_use: For a particular end-use (e.g. saline IV bag, pharmaceutical injection) - the solution form is what the user buys to use

notes: Applies Ch.29 Note 1(e). 'Safety/transport' solutions stay Ch.29; 'specific use' solutions move to the appropriate formulation chapter (Ch.30 for pharma, Ch.38 for industrial).

question_text: How is the coffee consumed?

value_labels.brewed_or_percolated: Must be brewed or percolated with hot water (filter through grounds)
value_labels.dissolves_directly: Dissolves directly in water without filtering (instant)
value_labels.ingredient_in_preparation: Used as a flavour base in another preparation (3-in-1, RTD beverage, dessert)

notes: Function confirms processing_state for Ch.09 vs Ch.21. Solubility-in-water is a useful runtime probe but downstream of extraction state.

question_text: What kind of vehicle or transport equipment is the product or part for?

value_labels.rail_tram: Railway or tramway vehicles or fixed rail equipment (Ch.86)
value_labels.road_motor_vehicle: Road motor vehicles, two-wheelers, tractors, trailers (Ch.87)

notes: Routes within Section XVII transport chapters. Each chapter has its own 'parts and accessories' rules and Section XVII Note 3 'solely or principally' test.

question_text: What kind of wood or plant material is the product made of?

value_labels.wood_panel: Wood panel (plywood, particleboard, MDF, OSB, veneer)
value_labels.plait_basket: Plaiting material (bamboo, rattan, straw, palm leaf, willow basketwork)

notes: Disambiguates within wood/cork/plaiting chapters (Ch.44 wood, Ch.45 cork, Ch.46 plaiting).

question_text: What natural fibre is the textile made from?

value_labels.other_vegetable_fibre: Other vegetable fibre - jute, flax, hemp, ramie, sisal, coir (Ch.53)

notes: Routes within natural-fibre textile chapters (Ch.50-53).

question_text: Is the product made of plastic or of rubber?

value_labels.plastic_thermoplastic: Plastic / polymer - rigid or flexible thermoplastic (PVC, PE, PP, PS, ABS, PET, PC, PA, etc.)
value_labels.rubber_synthetic: Synthetic rubber (SBR, NBR, EPDM, silicone rubber)

notes: Disambiguates Ch.39 (plastics, including thermosets) vs Ch.40 (rubber, natural and synthetic). Silicone elastomers go to Ch.40 even though chemically silicone; silicone resins/oils go to Ch.39 / Ch.34.

question_text: Where is the lamp/luminaire or furniture article designed to be used?

value_labels.outdoor_streetlight: Outdoor, street, garden or specialised commercial lighting
value_labels.medical_surgical: Medical, surgical or dental furniture (Ch.94 heading 9402)

notes: Routes within Ch.94 (furniture, lamps, lighting fittings).

question_text: In what form is the paper or paperboard product?

value_labels.rolls_or_sheets_blank: Rolls or sheets - blank, uncoated or simply coated (Ch.48 heading 4801-4811)
value_labels.other_articles: Other articles of paper (cups, plates, hygiene items, filter paper, etc.)

notes: Within Ch.48, form drives heading selection.

question_text: What is the end-use of the chemical preparation?

value_labels.essential_oil_aroma: Essential oil, resinoid or aroma chemical (Ch.33)

notes: Disambiguates Ch.32 (paints, dyes, tanning) vs Ch.33 (perfumes, cosmetics, essential oils). Both have similar 'preparation' structure.

question_text: What is the primary function of the chemical product?

value_labels.cleaning_solvent: Cleaning agent, solvent, polish (NOT soap - soaps are Ch.34)
value_labels.agricultural_chemical: Pesticide, herbicide, fungicide, plant growth regulator
value_labels.industrial_reagent: Industrial chemical reagent, additive or auxiliary

notes: Within Ch.38 (miscellaneous chemical products), function drives heading.

question_text: What is the primary material of the footwear's upper, and what of the sole?

value_labels.leather_upper_rubber_sole: Leather upper with rubber/plastic outer sole (6403)
value_labels.leather_upper_leather_sole: Leather upper with leather outer sole (6403)
value_labels.textile_upper_rubber_sole: Textile upper with rubber/plastic outer sole (6404)

notes: Within Ch.64, footwear heading is driven by upper material AND outer sole material combined.

question_text: In what form is the glass article?

value_labels.raw_glass_cullet: Glass in primary form (cullet, mass, balls, rods)
value_labels.technical_fibre_optical: Glass fibre, optical fibre, technical glass

notes: Within Ch.70, form drives heading.

question_text: What is the intended use of the article?

value_labels.toy_for_children: Toy intended for amusement of children (9503)

notes: Within Ch.95, intended use drives heading.

question_text: In what form is the inorganic chemical?

value_labels.element_pure: Pure element (e.g. iodine, sulphur, phosphorus, halogen gas)
value_labels.acid_or_base: Inorganic acid or base (HCl, H2SO4, NaOH)

notes: Within Ch.28, sub-chapter routing depends on chemical form.

question_text: What is the end-use of the precious-metal or stone article?

value_labels.coin_or_bullion: Coin, bullion bar, or investment-grade metal (7118/7108)
value_labels.industrial_technical: Industrial or technical use (e.g. platinum catalyst, electronic contact)
value_labels.unworked_natural_stone: Unworked or worked natural / synthetic precious or semi-precious stone (7102-7104)

notes: Within Ch.71, intended use drives heading.

question_text: Is the product made of natural stone, cement-based material, or ceramic?

value_labels.stone_natural: Natural stone (granite, marble, sandstone, slate) - Ch.68
value_labels.cement_concrete: Cement, concrete or artificial-stone composition - Ch.68
value_labels.ceramic_unfired_or_refractory: Refractory ceramic or building brick - Ch.69 heading 6901-6906
value_labels.ceramic_tableware_sanitary: Ceramic tableware, sanitary ware, or fine porcelain - Ch.69 heading 6907-6914
value_labels.abrasive_or_mica: Abrasive product, mica, or asbestos-based - Ch.68

notes: Disambiguates Ch.68 (stone/cement/abrasives) from Ch.69 (ceramics).
